newsitem.title: USA: Eott sees Q2 net loss below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Eott sees Q2 net loss below estimates.

text.p: EOTT Energy Partners LP said Monday it expects to report a second quarter net loss in the range of $6-$7 million, significantly lower than analysts' current estimates.
The crude oil and refined products marketer said the expected loss results from lower gross margins due to grade and basis differentials in the North American crude gathering business.
First Call had estimated the company's second quarter per share loss at $0.02.
In the second quarter of 1996, the company reported a net profit of $10 million or $0.52 a share on revenues of $1.69 billion.

Phil Hawk, president and chief executive officer of the company, said that in the second quarter of 1997, industry-wide crude oil margins hit some of the lowest levels in the five years, but improved towards the end of the period.
He said the company has made "substantial progress" in renegotiating lease crude oil contracts to reflect current market conditions.
The company said distributions on common units in the seocnd quarter will amount to $5.6 million, which it expects to pay without support from Enron Corp, its indirect parent.

Enron previously committed to provide cash support to permit EOTT to make distributions to unitholders if there is an earnings shortgfall. That support extends through the second quarter ending March 31, 1998, for up to $29 million, of which $20 million is currently available, it said.
